transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood), Aisha (CTO), Marco (Lead ML), Priya (PM), Tomoya (Robotics SW)

Auto Summary: POC scoping for telemetry extraction + command understanding. Discussed success criteria, sample size, shortlist of open models, quantization/latency targets, deployment (Dedicated vs Private VPC), security needs. Action items and next steps captured.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Aisha (Kestrel): hi, aisha here, marco, priya and tomoya with me. thanks for scheduling.
[00:10] Jordan: awesome. goals for today: nail down success criteria, rough workload sizing, and a model shortlist so we can scope the bench. Sofia, want to add?
[00:18] Sofia (Redwood SE): yeah i'll also capture deployment touchpoints — whether you want Dedicated reserved gpus or private vpc on prem, and note security ask like kms/sso.
[00:25] Marco: to be clear our immediate need is twofold: 1) short voice/text control commands translated into robot actions (often 3-12 tokens), and 2) parsing free-form telemetry logs into structured fields — battery, motor temp, error codes. both need multilingual support (en, ja, es).
[00:40] Tomoya: and we have intermittent connectivity in the field, so an on-prem inference option or private vpc is likely. don't want cloud-only for sensitive logs.
[00:48] Jordan: understood. let's capture success criteria — what does success look like for your team?
[00:52] Priya: from product POV — demoable POC in 6 weeks that shows command latency <100ms median, extraction F1 >=0.95 on key fields, and qualitative pass on hallucination for safety-critical commands.
[01:10] Marco: technicallly we'd accept 90% if latency is much better but target is 95% for extraction. throughput wise we see ~1k control commands/day per 100 robots, bursts up to 200rps at our on-prem gateway during tests.
[01:30] Sofia: good: those numbers let us size GPUs and batching. for <100ms median on short prompts, we'll need models that can run at low-precision quantized kernels or smaller specialized variants.
[01:42] Aisha: can you talk through model options? we prefer open models but need to understand tradeoffs for multilingual accuracy and hallucination.
[01:50] Jordan: absolutely. initial shortlist we recommend to evaluate in the POC: a) Mosaic-Edge-13B (good latency after quant; decent multilingual), b) Llama-3-34B-q8f or similar 34b quant variant (strong general quality, heavier), c) Redwing-7B (smaller, fast, domain-tune friendly), d) Mistral-family 7B dense for multilingual — and optionally a larger 70B variant for a quality ceiling test.
[02:25] Marco: quick callout — we have seen Mistral drop in non-english for some robotics vocab, anxious about japanese.
[02:33] Sofia: noted. our POC will include per-language evals. we'll also test bilingual prompts and zero-shot commands.
[02:40] Jordan: also flag that a 34B will likely need Dedicated reserved capacity to meet the latency SLO without aggressive batching; a 7-13B family can probably hit targets on a single A100 or H100 with q4/q8 quant.
[02:55] Tomoya: what's q4 vs q8 in practice? is accuracy hit big?
[02:58] Sofia: q4 may slightly hurt extraction F1 but often acceptable; q8f gives better fidelity. We'll run microbenchmarks. keep in mind kernel selection and KV cache behavior for sessioned commands matters for latency.
[03:15] Jordan: let's talk benchmarks — what do you want measured?
[03:18] Priya: latency distribution (p50/p90/p99), extraction F1 per field and aggregated, false-positive rate for hallucinated commands, throughput under burst, memory/instantiation time for model swap, and cost per 1k commands.
[03:33] Jordan: perfect. Sofia, can you sketch a test harness?
[03:36] Sofia: we'll create three harness tests: 1) short command latency bench (1-12 tokens) across languages; 2) telemetry extraction bench with labeled corpus (entity-level F1); 3) safety/hallucination probe — model asked ambiguous or out-of-domain to see tendency to invent. each test will run across shortlist models and quant settings.
[03:58] Marco: what sort of sample sizes? we can provide ~1k telemetry lines, 500 command examples, and we'll augment with synthetic variants.
[04:05] Sofia: that should be fine. more data helps, but for POC that corpus is workable. we'll also do some stress bursts to simulate gateway.
[04:12] Aisha: security — we need SOC2-type audit logs, SSO via SAML, and KMS for keys. private deployment must support our HSM or bring-your-own-kms.
[04:22] Jordan: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; Dedicated (hosted) can be configured with strict tenancy but may not meet your air-gap needs. we'll share the security pack.
[04:32] Marco: any customs or gotchas for on-prem GPU drivers? we run mixed nvidia and ampere series, some older T4s in legacy labs.
[04:40] Evan (Redwood): we'll include a compatibility matrix; our runtime can target a range but performance will vary. for latency SLOs we recommend H100 or 80GB-class GPUs for heavier models, 3090/T4 et al will be slower.
[04:55] Priya: timeline? you said 6 weeks earlier. break that down.
[04:58] Jordan: proposed plan: week 0 (this week) — finalize success criteria and corpus; week 1 — initial bench runs with 1-2 model configs; week 2-3 — iterate on quant/serving config and language tests; week 4 — heavy stress runs, on-prem smoke; week 5 — final tuned runs and cost/ops review; week 6 — demo + sign-off.
[05:22] Marco: doable. any risk on model licensing or export controls?
[05:26] Jordan: all open models we'll test are permissive for internal use; we'll flag specific licenses. export controls generally not an issue for inference, but we'll double-check.
[05:34] Tomoya: curious about fallback behavior — if Dedicated pool is saturated, can requests route to smaller models?
[05:39] Sofia: yes — Redwood routing supports policy-based fallback to cheaper/compatible model variants by latency or cost. we can set automatic fallbacks during bursts to maintain availability and avoid queueing.
[05:52] Priya: and observability? we need token-level cost, per-route latency, and per-prompt tracing to debug bad parses.
[05:59] Jordan: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdown, per-model dashboard and traces; we can expose logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud forwarder.
[06:10] Marco: ok, let's be explicit about quantitative acceptance: p50 <100ms, p90 <200ms, extraction F1 >=0.95 on core fields, hallucination <2% on safety probes, and deployable in our private VPC.
[06:28] Jordan: copying that to action items.
[06:30] Aisha: competitor question — we've evaluated Inferly previously; what differentiates Redwood?
[06:35] Jordan: two big pieces: production-first serving runtime (kernel selection, continuous batching, KV caching) and consistent interface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so you don't rewrite evaluation or rollout logic when you move to on-prem. also built-in rollouts and quality regressions tied to prompts.
[06:54] Marco: any example numbers on cost delta between 13B q8 vs 34B q8?
[06:58] Evan: ballpark: 13B q8 on Dedicated can be 2-3x cheaper per token and 2-4x faster in cold starts versus 34B, but quality tradeoffs vary. we'll include a cost/perf sheet.
[07:10] Priya: what about multilingual — do you recommend fine-tuning or prompt engineering first?
[07:15] Sofia: start with prompt/task-specific tuning + eval; if gaps persist we can do a small adapter or LoRA on telemetry examples. fine-tuning full model is heavier but doable if needed.
[07:26] Jordan: ok wrapping up — recap of owners and timelines.
[07:30] (brief cross-talk)
[07:35] Jordan: Jordan to send pricing and security docs; Sofia to stand up bench harness and run baseline; Marco to upload telemetry corpus; Priya to share stakeholder list. everyone okay with the 6-week target?
[07:45] Aisha: yes, let's aim for that.
[07:48] Tomoya: one more note — for local inference we may want to test INT8 hires quant on our edge boxes, will that be part of the bench?
[07:55] Sofia: yes we can include INT8 and q4/q8 profiles in the bench matrix, but note INT8 needs kernel support and may change accuracy.
[08:05] Marco: any additional data you need from us today?
[08:08] Jordan: the items listed in next_steps; main thing is telemetry + command samples. also if you can indicate expected peak concurrent robots for the stress runs that helps.
[08:18] Priya: we'll provide peak concurrency (up to 250) and a list of safety-critical command types.
[08:22] Jordan: great. we'll follow up with calendar invite for the bench planning and the pricing doc. thanks everyone.
[08:28] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript: there are some transcription artifacts (model names sometimes shortened; "q8f" referred to as "q eight f") and speaker overlaps.

Bench plan (brief):
- Models to test: Mosaic-Edge-13B (q4/q8), Llama-3-34B-q8f, Redwing-7B (domain-tune), Mistral-7B, optional Llama-3-70B as quality ceiling.
- Tests: latency bench (tokens/short prompts), extraction F1 on labeled telemetry, hallucination probe, burst throughput stress.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, end-to-end parse time, per-field F1, hallucination rate, cost per 1k commands.

References shared: security packet link (doc: /redwood/security-pack.pdf - placeholder), pricing spreadsheet link (sheet: /redwood/pricing/kestrel-dedicated.xlsx - placeholder).
